comparison: Perfect agreement on particle picking application (C91-C115). Both evaluations recognize this as a convincing demonstration of the software's utility, with OpenEval noting the quantitative validation (44 Å resolution matching manual picking) and peer reviewers explicitly acknowledging the comparison with previously published manual picking.

Strong agreement on model interaction system (C66-C83). Both evaluations recognize this as a valuable feature for reducing false positives. OpenEval provides detailed technical assessment of the implementation, while peer reviewers explicitly praise the heuristic rules and interactive merging capabilities.

Strong agreement on architecture comparison experiment (C49-C62, C145-C148). Both evaluations accept the comparative analysis as useful. OpenEval emphasizes the finding that loss values don't correlate perfectly with quality, while peer reviewers highlight the value of comparing multiple CNNs in one environment.

Agreement on background context about cryoET workflows (C84-C90, C116-C119). Both evaluations accept these as established field knowledge. OpenEval explicitly labels them as 'well-accepted facts,' while peer reviewers implicitly accept by not challenging the contextual framing.

Substantial agreement on software features and capabilities (C4-C35, C140-C144, C166-C170). Both evaluations support the comprehensive functionality. OpenEval provides detailed technical validation, while peer reviewers explicitly praise it as 'a valuable tool' with 'comprehensive functionality.' Peer review also includes model repository claims (C38-C41) that OpenEval evaluates separately.

Agreement on model repository (C38-C42, C142). OpenEval evaluates this separately as a distinct feature with verifiable claims about initial content. Peer reviewers include this within overall software assessment and specifically identify the online repository as a 'distinguishing factor' and strength.

Agreement on bacterial cilia segmentation (C120-C127). Both evaluations accept this demonstration. OpenEval emphasizes biological validation through ribosome exclusion zone identification, while peer reviewers note the visual analysis approach without challenging validity.

Agreement on mitochondrial segmentation (C128-C130). Both evaluations support this demonstration. OpenEval highlights the discriminatory power in distinguishing membrane types, while peer reviewers group this with other cellular segmentation examples as evidence of capability.

Agreement on complex viral segmentation (C131-C139). Both evaluations accept this as the most complex demonstration. OpenEval notes the imprecision in annotation time reporting ('some hours'), while peer reviewers accept the visual demonstration without methodological concerns.

Divergence on software gap claims (C3, C12-C15). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting these are subjective assessments and that acknowledgment of similar tools (C42-C45) contradicts claims of a clear deficit. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, implicitly accepting the motivation by characterizing the work as addressing a real need without challenging the framing.

Divergence on model transferability speculation (C36-C37). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, explicitly noting C37 is labeled as speculation and lacks systematic validation. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, accepting the premise as rationale for the model repository they identify as a key strength.

Agreement on acknowledgment of prior work (C42-C45). Both evaluations support these claims. OpenEval notes proper citations and awareness of existing tools but lack of detailed comparison. Peer reviewers implicitly accept by not challenging the contextual framing.

Agreement on methodology documentation (C160-C164). Both evaluations support these factual statements about methods. OpenEval notes proper citations to previous work and standard packages. Peer reviewers implicitly accept as standard reporting without raising concerns.

Agreement on hardware specifications (C156). Both evaluations support this as factual reporting. OpenEval identifies it as specific information for reproducibility. Peer reviewers implicitly accept within overall technical details.

Agreement on practical recommendations (C151, C159). Both evaluations support these claims. OpenEval notes they are reasonable suggestions based on experience though not experimentally validated. Peer reviewers implicitly accept within the comparative analysis context.

Agreement on training monitoring capabilities (C63-C65). OpenEval includes these within comprehensive software features assessment. Peer reviewers implicitly accept as part of overall functionality praised for 'streamlined approaches' and 'methods to refine outputs.'

Agreement on field context and motivation (C1-C2, C10-C11). Both evaluations support these background claims. OpenEval labels as 'well-accepted facts in the field.' Peer reviewers implicitly accept by recognizing the software addresses real needs in particle picking and segmentation.

Partial overlap on acceleration claims (C6-C7 in peer R10 only). Peer reviewers validate acceleration claims through demonstrated applications, noting software 'promises substantially faster results.' OpenEval does not separately evaluate these specific claims but addresses related efficiency claims in application demonstrations.
